newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Pacific caps turnaround year with profit.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific caps turnaround year with profit.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd. reported a strong fourth-quarter profit on Monday, showing a convincing turnaround from a big loss a year earlier.
"All our businesses contributed to the improvement. We're working to build on this momentum in 1997," CP Chief Executive David O'Brien said in a statement.

The Montreal-based railway, energy and shipping conglomerate posted net earnings of C$257 million ($190 million) or C74 cents (55 cents) a share in the fourth quarter, compared with a net loss of C$990 million ($733 million) or C$2.90 ($2.10) a share in the year earlier period.
Sales were C$2.5 billion ($1.85 billion) in the fourth quarter, compared with year earlier C$2.1 billion ($1.55 billion).
For the full year, CP posted a net profit of C$829 million, ($613.5 million) or C$2.41 ($1.78) a share, compared with a net loss of C$824 million ($610 million) or C$2.41 ($1.78) a share in 1995.
CP's 1995 net loss came after net charges of C$740 million ($548 million), including a restructuring charge at Canadian Pacific Railway of C$704 million ($521 million) in the fourth quarter.
Sales in 1996 were C$8.7 billion ($6.4 billion), versus C$7.5 billion ($5.5 billion) in 1995.
During the year, CP Rail improved its operating income by 39 percent, mainly by cutting costs. The railway reduced its average number of active employees in 1996 by 1,700 to 21,173.
CP said CP Rail would benefit in 1997 from the full realization of its cost-cutting initiatives as well as efforts to rationalize its rail network across Canada.
CP stock was up C55 cents to C$36.80 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday and rose 50 cents to $27.375 in New York.
